title: Tax and Jurisdictional Compliance
answer: Structuring, transfer pricing, research credits, indirect tax and audit defence.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Tax Structuring and Planning
children.blurb: Tax structuring and planning is the practice of arranging a company's legal entities, transactions, and cash flows so that tax outcomes follow the commercial substance and the applicable rules.

children.name: Transfer Pricing
children.blurb: Transfer pricing is the set of rules and practices that govern how related entities within a multinational group price transactions with each other, including goods, services, royalties, loans, and cost allocations.

children.name: Research Credits from Engineering Records
children.blurb: Research credits from engineering records covers the use of engineering artifacts to support claims for research and development tax credits.

children.name: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
children.blurb: Sales, use, and value added tax are transaction taxes that apply to the transfer of goods and services.

children.name: Audit Defence and Controversy
children.blurb: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of responding to tax authority inquiries, audits, assessments, appeals, and mutual agreement procedures across jurisdictions.

sections.body: Tax and jurisdictional compliance is the work of keeping a company's tax position defensible across every country it operates in. In artificial intelligence this has become a live operational problem rather than a year end exercise, because models are trained in one place, served from data centres in several others, and sold to customers everywhere. Teams now use software to map where value is created, where servers sit, and which entity books the revenue, then test whether those three answers agree. The same tools read engineering logs to support claims about development activity, and they watch transaction data for indirect tax as it is invoiced. The field is less about filing returns and more about holding a consistent story that survives scrutiny from more than one authority at once.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The mechanics are largely solved. Routine returns, rate lookups and threshold monitoring are automated well, and document review for audit preparation has improved sharply. What is not solved is the underlying disagreement about where artificial intelligence value is created, since tax authorities in different countries can reach different conclusions from the same facts. Transfer pricing for intangible assets remains contested, and research credit claims still depend on records that many engineering teams do not keep in an auditable form. The honest limit is that no tool resolves a genuine conflict between jurisdictions. It can only show the exposure clearly and produce the evidence faster.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the order in which a company usually meets the problem. Tax Structuring and Planning sets the entity and flow design that everything else depends on, so a reader starts there to understand the shape of the position. Transfer Pricing takes that structure and asks whether the prices between related entities hold up, which is where most cross border disputes begin. Research Credits from Engineering Records is the evidence page, showing how development logs and commit history become a claim. Sales, Use and Value Added Tax covers the transaction level obligations that arise as products are actually sold. Audit Defence and Controversy is the end point, where a position is tested and the earlier pages either support it or fail it.
